note: New cases written after the round 2 prompt fix and never used to tune any prompt. Fictional products, companies and people only (Crumbline by Oakhollow Software for bakeries; Shiftnest by Bramblegate for care homes; Pallet Pilot for small warehouses); none of the Pawpath wording is reused. The answer key is the required, framework and traps lists in this file, written and committed before any model call. required and framework are copied unchanged from fixtures.json so the checks are the same as the tuned set. traps are extra fixed text-pattern checks for the weak shapes EVALS.md reported (a cycle length called standard, an assumed design effect with no label, named outside sources, a penetration figure with no market size, invented contact details); a trap that matches is a miss.

required.label: executive summary
required.note: Heading such as Executive Summary / Summary / TL;DR, OR (as the prompt literally asks for "a one-paragraph executive summary") a prose paragraph of 300+ characters between the H1 and the first ## heading. Widened after the one-module smoke run, which had the paragraph but no heading.

sections.label: Problem Statement
sections.value: Bakeries on Crumbline take repeat wholesale orders (cafes, delis) by WhatsApp and re-key them every week. Owners told us re-keying takes most of Sunday evening. 1 in 9 wholesale orders last quarter had a wrong quantity.

sections.label: Target Users
sections.value: Owners and shift leads at independent bakeries with one to three shops, plus their wholesale buyers. Buyers order between 9 pm and 5 am.

sections.label: Goals & Success Metrics
sections.value: Cut wholesale order errors to under 1 in 40. Make weekly order entry feel quick for owners. Keep buyers off the phone.

sections.label: Scope & Constraints
sections.value: In scope: a standing order a buyer can edit until a cut-off the bakery sets. Out of scope: invoicing and delivery routing. Must work offline on the shop tablet. Beta with 7 bakeries before the spring menu change in March.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Oakhollow Software sells Crumbline to independent bakeries. 238 paying bakeries, $612K ARR. Net revenue retention last year was 94%. Bakeries that set up wholesale ordering in their first month stay far longer than those that do not.

sections.label: Goals & Objectives
sections.value: Get new bakeries to wholesale ordering in their first month. Win back bakeries that downgraded to the free plan. Ship the offline tablet mode.

sections.label: Constraints & Considerations
sections.value: The quarter runs 6 January to 28 March. Team: 5 engineers, 1 designer, 2 customer success leads. No new hires until April.

sections.value: Ten calls with registered managers of small care homes who started using Shiftnest this year. Seven of ten ran rotas in a spreadsheet emailed to staff each week.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Shiftnest will launch a payroll export that sends approved hours to three payroll providers on 1 April, the start of the new tax year. 126 care homes have asked for it. Hours worked feed directly into staff pay.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Pallet Pilot is slotting software that tells small third-party warehouses (one site, 5,000 to 40,000 pallet spaces) where to put incoming stock. Today these warehouses use the slotting rules in their warehouse management system, a planner's spreadsheet, or the floor lead's memory.

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: Unique attributes: learns pick frequency from the existing WMS export with no integration project, re-slots in small nightly moves instead of a big weekend reshuffle, and shows the floor lead why each move is suggested. Customers say the nightly moves are why the floor accepts it.

sections.label: Context & Background
sections.value: Crumbline lets bakeries print shelf labels. We want to test showing a 'baked today' time on the label against the current price-only label. The metric we care about is the share of each day's bake sold by closing. Today that share is 82% on average.

sections.label: Key Inputs
sections.value: 238 bakeries, 412 shops in total. Labels are printed per shop, so the test must be split by shop, not by customer. Shops range from 40 to 900 items baked a day.
